{{nihongo|'''Ōmiwa Shrine'''|大神神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (おおみわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Hanaike, Ichinomiya, Aichi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and styles itself as {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity is the following{{Sfn|大神神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.
* '''{{ill|Ōmononushi|fr|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|mni|ꯑꯣꯃꯣꯅꯣꯅꯨꯁꯤ|ru|Омононуси|simple|Ōmononushi|zh|大物主|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Kami}}'''
*: A deity worshipped by the {{ill|Miwa clan|Q11438330|qid=Q11438330}} (Miwa clan), and the deity of {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|Q705542|qid=Q705542}} (Sakurai, Nara){{Sfn|大神神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

Apart from Ōmononushi, a theory identifies the deity as Ōmiwatsune-no-Mikoto (seen in the '{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}'), suggesting common ancestry between the {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}} and this shrine’s worship clan{{Sfn|大神神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

=== History ===
Founding unknown. Until the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} it was called '''Sanmyōjin''' or '''Sannomiya Myōjin'''{{Sfn|大神神社（平凡社）|1981年}}. It is identified with “Ōmiwa Shrine, Myojin-grand” in Nakashima District, Owari Province, in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'{{Sfn|大神神社（平凡社）|1981年}}. Depending on manuscript, name appears as “Ōkami-gami-sha” or “Taisha.”

Unlike other Myojin-grand shrines, it is not listed in the Myojin-festival section of the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' temporary rites, leading to a view that “Myojin-grand” in Jinmyōchō is an interpolation. The affirmative view infers it joined Myojin-grand rank after completion of '{{ill|Jōgan-shiki|Q11634547|qid=Q11634547}}' and temporary ritual codes{{Sfn|大神神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

In Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}) May, it was ranked {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gōsha}} under the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=modern shrine rank system}}{{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912年}}. Today it claims Owari Ichinomiya and belongs to the National Ichinomiya Association (though generally Owari Ichinomiya is {{ill|Masumida Shrine|el|Ιερό Μασουμίντα|eu|Masumida santutegia|fr|Masumida-jinja|ja|真清田神社|zh|真清田神社|qid=Q705916}}). The shrine side argues Masumida and Ōmiwa were paired shrines and both became Ichinomiya.

=== Divine ranks ===
All written as “Ōmiwa Myōjin.” Rank varies by manuscript.
* Senior First Rank ('Owari no Kuni Jinmyōchō' Atsuta text)
* Junior First Rank ('Owari no Kuni Jinmyōchō' Mizō-in and Tenbun texts)
* Senior Second Rank Upper ('Owari no Kuni Jinmyōchō' Kōnomiya text)

=== Sessha and massha ===
Current six:
* Rokusho-sha
* Mishima-sha
* Hakusan-sha
* Shinmei-sha
* Shōkon-sha
* Susano-sha

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Ichinomiya City-designated Tangible Cultural Property ===
* One pair of wooden komainu (sculpture)

=== Other ===
As shrine treasures, there are 3 swords kept at Ichinomiya City Museum.
